answer: Each identity runs one satellite ground station in a willow clearing and must decode a fresh nonce in a passing satellite signal within 10 minutes, posting a hash whose Doppler curve matches that site's coordinates. Verifiers compare the curve to orbital ephemeris and a quill-signed site register; a mismatched or replayed decode loses a 5-coin bond and the slot. One receiver yields one Doppler profile, so 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 kits at 380 dollars each (380,000 dollars), 1,000 sites over 2 km apart, and 15 dollars monthly power each. Trade-off: agents without clear sky view qualify slowly.
